title: Comparing objects and non-objects throws type errors
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.4.1.stable.arch_linux

### System information

Godot v4.4.1.stable unknown - Arch Linux

### Issue description

Similar to #11430, I'd like to be able to do
`Object.new() != "string"`
and get `true` rather than a request by Godot to add an unnecessary type test prior to comparing the values. I really don't see the point. And since it throws an exception it means it can be fixed without breaking backward compatibility since AFAIK there's no try-catch mechanics in GDScript, ie you can't make use of a type error, only try to avoid producing one.

I know the 'type-strict' equality checks were done on purpose and it's not an oversight (cf https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/85641c545bedbdb703ad923306786afe5c312110), however I just don't understand the rationale (and I couldn't find a link to the discussion mentioned, so IDK what motivated that change). To me it serves no purpose and just forces end users to add unnecessary boilerplate. Right now my only viable option as someone who hates code redundancy is to create a new and inevitably ugly function wrapper in my toolbox to encapsulate that unnecessary boilerplate that is required of me, just to have a type-proof equality operator.

Putting it another way, if I have a function that takes two Variants, I'd like to be able to use a GDScript operator to get the boolean that will tell me whether they're equal or not, without having to jump through type hoops. Having no equality operator with type signature `(Variant, Variant) -> bool` doesn't make sense to me.

Being forced to write `typeof(a) == typeof(b) and a == b` every time I'm comparing Variants is gonna get old very quickly. Admittedly and thankfully, it's pretty rare, I avoid using variants as much as possible, which is why it's the first time I've encountered this issue in over a year of coding in GDScript. It still feels like it shouldn't be needed at all.

### Steps to reproduce

`if Object.new() != "string": print("gonna crash before it reaches this")`

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

`if Object.new() != "string": print("gonna crash before it reaches this")`
